rich_summary: This section marks the formal beginning of the Bhagavad Gita within the Mahabharata. Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to describe what happens when the Kauravas and Pandavas assemble on the sacred battlefield of Kurukshetra. Sanjaya recounts how Duryodhana, seeing the well‑organized Pandava army, approaches his teacher Drona and lists the powerful warriors on both sides, revealing both confidence and anxiety. The grandsire Bhishma sounds his conch, triggering a thunderous chorus of war instruments from both armies. Krishna and Arjuna answer with their own divine conches. As the battle is about to begin, Arjuna asks Krishna to place his chariot between the armies so he can observe those he must fight. Seeing relatives, teachers, and friends on both sides, Arjuna is overwhelmed with grief and moral doubt, setting the stage for the philosophical dialogue of the Gita.

highlight_spans.why: Dhritarashtra’s anxious questioning frames the entire scene and introduces the moral and emotional tension before the battle.
The narrative transition into the Bhagavad Gita proper, where the battlefield setting becomes the stage for philosophical teaching.
Duryodhana’s catalog of warriors highlights the immense power on both sides and subtly reveals his concern about the Pandava forces.
The sounding of conches and instruments symbolizes the formal commencement of battle and the dramatic tension of the moment.
Arjuna’s emotional collapse upon seeing his relatives marks the pivotal moral crisis that prompts the teachings of the Gita.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhishma standing in his chariot blowing a mighty conch while thousands of warriors, elephants, and banners fill the battlefield of Kurukshetra.
Krishna driving Arjuna’s white-horsed chariot between the two massive armies as conches echo across the field.
Arjuna lowering the Gandiva bow, trembling as he recognizes teachers, elders, and relatives standing on both sides of the battlefield.
